answer: A practical defense is hardware-beacon identity: every agent binds its account to the unique drift signature of its machine's quartz crystal oscillator — no two clocks tick alike, so the beacon cannot be cloned in software. Each epoch the agent publishes a signed timing signal anchored to that drift, and peers reject duplicates sharing one beacon. Like an opal, the ledger of beacons is layered and one-of-a-kind. An attacker must buy a physical machine per fake identity, turning a nearly free botnet into a warehouse of costly hardware.
